newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak govt changes budget funding sources - FinMin.
newsitem.headline: Slovak govt changes budget funding sources - FinMin.

text.p: The Slovak government is changing the way it will raise funds to cover some budget- financed projects to bank credits -- including foreign loans -- from the originally-planned method of using bond issues.

"The government has reconsidered some of its projects and decided to change the way of financing them, turning to cheaper funds from bank loans," Deputy Finance Minister Peter Stanek told journalists after a regular government session on Tuesday.
Stanek said Slovakia was offered cheap loans from abroad with interest rate of 60 basis points over London Interbank Offered rate (LIBOR) and the postponement of repayment for five years.
He said the cabinet has also reconsidered some of its infrastructure projects, but would not give further details.

The government's ambitious budget investment projects have often been criticised -- even by the central bank -- as too expansive, and could possibly endanger the financing of the budget deficit itself.

The original 1997 budget forecast a 36.9 billion crown deficit (after a 25.5 billion crown shortfall in 1996), with multibillion crown allocations for infrastructure projects, including 14 billion crowns for covering motorway construction.
The budget deficit totalled 4.692 billion crowns in the first four months of this year, up from 3.450 billion crowns in the first quarter of 1997.
Earlier on Tuesday, ratings agency Standard and Poor's affirmed its triple-'B'-minus long-term foreign currency and its single-'A' long-term local currency ratings on the Slovak Republic.

The outlook on both ratings remains stable. Also, Standard & Poor's has affirmed its 'A-1' short-term local currency rating on the republic and has assigned an 'A-3' short-term foreign currency rating.
